findings.title: No fallback/error handling if neither user storage nor local credential provider accept the credential
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential relies on user.credentialManager().updateCredential returning false to fall back to the local provider, but it doesn't check whether recoveryCodeCredentialProvider itself is null (e.g. if the 'keycloak-recovery-authn-codes' provider isn't registered) or handle the case where createCredential fails. Unlike createOTPCredential, there's no return value or validation step, so callers cannot detect failures, potentially leaving the user without a recovery credential silently.

findings.title: getCredentials ignores password credential and uses raw List type
findings.body: The newly added getCredentials() method only returns OTP and recovery-code credentials, omitting the password credential entirely, which may be inconsistent with how getCredentials is expected to enumerate all credentials for a user. Also, JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class) with no generic type parameter produces unchecked raw List<Object>, which could cause ClassCastException issues downstream when code expects List<String>.

findings.title: No null/format validation on required action form parameters
findings.body: generatedCodesString, generatedAtTimeString are used directly (e.g. generatedAtTimeString.equals(...), Long.valueOf(generatedAtTimeString), generatedCodesString.split(",")) without null checks. If these hidden fields are missing from the form submission (e.g. due to a malformed request), this will throw an NPE or NumberFormatException instead of being handled gracefully, which was already a pre-existing issue but is now exercised via the new createRecoveryCodesCredential flow without added safety.
